react_result.final_narrative_text: The nine-metabolite panel is dominated by tryptophan catabolism, with overwhelming cross-paradigm consensus for the Tryptophan metabolism pathway. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked KEGG:map00380 first (FDR 8.86e-19, fold enrichment 875.7, 7 of 9 inputs hit), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 as the top hit (p = 5.41e-09, 6 of 9 inputs hit). The two tools share six driver metabolites (L-tryptophan, serotonin, melatonin, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, indoleacetaldehyde, tryptamine); RaMP additionally captured quinolinic acid in the broader map00380 entry. WikiPathways WP:WP465 (Tryptophan metabolism) scored FDR 4.15e-15, and the IDO metabolic pathway WP:WP5414 was rank 6 (FDR 8.38e-09), reflecting the kynurenine-branch metabolites (3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid). Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis (REACT:R-HSA-209931) was rank 7 (FDR 2.02e-08, fold enrichment 1351). Ureidosuccinic acid and O-phosphoethanolamine contributed to the broad Amino acid metabolism and Biochemical pathways hits but did not enrich specifically for tryptophan metabolism. L-Tryptophan is the pathway entry substrate; serotonin and melatonin are the downstream biogenic-amine products; 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and quinolinic acid represent the neuroactive kynurenine-branch intermediates. The convergent signal across three independent tools (RaMP, MetaboAnalystR, and WikiPathways ORA) with FDR scores spanning 1e-8 to 1e-19 establishes this as a robust, multi-arm perturbation of tryptophan catabolism.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment methods converged on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this nine-metabolite panel. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism first (FDR 8.86e-19, 7 of 9 inputs), while MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 as the top hit (p-value 5.41e-09, 6 of 9 inputs). Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis identified MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 (p-value 0.000168). The convergent signal across ORA and m/z-direct methods establishes this as a robust perturbation of Tryptophan metabolism. The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 8.38e-09) captured 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid, and L-tryptophan, while the Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.02e-08) captured L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin. Ureidosuccinic acid and O-phosphoethanolamine enriched for the broader Amino acid metabolism pathway (WP:WP3925, FDR 5.82e-11) and were absent from the tryptophan-specific KEGG entry. L-Tryptophan is the pathway entry substrate with the broadest signal across arms (serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid). Melatonin and serotonin are downstream biogenic-amine products linked through the REACT:R-HSA-209931 arm.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent enrichment methods converged on tryptophan metabolism as the dominant perturbed pathway in this nine-metabolite panel. RaMP multi-DB ORA ranked KEGG:map00380 Tryptophan metabolism first (FDR 8.86e-19, 7 of 9 inputs), while MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00380 as the top hit (p-value 5.41e-09, 6 of 9 inputs). Mummichog m/z-direct activity analysis identified MUMM:tryptophan_metabolism at rank 0 (p-value 0.000168). The convergent signal across ORA and m/z-direct methods establishes this as a robust perturbation of Tryptophan metabolism. The IDO metabolic pathway (WP:WP5414, FDR 8.38e-09) captured 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid, and L-tryptophan, while the Serotonin and melatonin biosynthesis pathway (REACT:R-HSA-209931, FDR 2.02e-08) captured L-tryptophan, serotonin, and melatonin. Ureidosuccinic acid and O-phosphoethanolamine enriched for the broader Amino acid metabolism pathway (WP:WP3925, FDR 5.82e-11) and were absent from the tryptophan-specific KEGG entry. L-Tryptophan is the pathway entry substrate with the broadest signal across arms (serotonin, melatonin, tryptamine, indoleacetaldehyde, 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid, quinolinic acid). Melatonin and serotonin are downstream biogenic-amine products linked through the REACT:R-HSA-209931 arm.
